Subject: Residency consent & temporary cross-region egress for onboarding

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security and privacy team need a concise description of Redwood's approach to region pinning (we're targeting EU for production). Two concrete asks from the DPO:

1) Does Redwood enforce physical residency (data at rest + inference) to the EU exclusively, or is there a documented transient cross-region egress policy for failover/maintenance?
2) If transient cross-region processing occurs, what is the maximum duration for a window where data may be routed outside the EU, and how is that documented in the DPA?
3) Are KMS keys customer-managed for EU-only residency projects? If not, what controls exist and where is the KMS handoff documented?
4) Updated subprocessor roster/timeline — we need an ETA to include in our DPA addendum.

We're preparing an internal checklist for our legal ops team and would appreciate a short written summary + any runbook or telemetry artifacts you can share.

Best,

Hi Erik — thanks for the clear list. Summarizing our posture below and attaching a short operational runbook: residency_runbook_v1.pdf. Markus (Legal) and Ben (Ops) are looped in to add legal language and operational SLAs.

Short answers up front:
- Region pinning: project-level region affinity pins both storage and inference traffic to selected region (EU). We provide EU-only placement for customer data sets when requested and validated in onboarding.
- Transient cross-region processing: permitted only in two controlled cases — (a) zonal/region failover or (b) scheduled maintenance with prior consent. Windows are timeboxed and audited.
- Max duration: standard practice is "up to 72 hours" for emergency failover with automated re-synchronization; scheduled maintenance windows are agreed in advance and typically <= 24 hours unless otherwise approved.
- KMS: customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported for Private and Dedicated customers; hosted customers can opt-in for split-key/escrow models. KMS handoff and key-wrapping boundaries are documented in the runbook and the proposed DPA clause.
- Subprocessors: we publish a rolling roster; new subprocessor activations are disclosed 30 days prior to activation unless emergency. ETA for the current roster update: Ben will confirm below.

Next steps:
- Ben: can you attach the transient_egress_playbook and confirm telemetry retention for audit logs?
- Markus: please review and suggest DPA clause language for the 72-hour transient-evidence requirement (we can surface as an addendum).
- Erik/Priya/legalops: confirm whether Medico requires a shorter window or additional contractual language (e.g., permanent EU-only clause).

Thanks — happy to schedule a 30 min call if it's easier to walk through the runbook.

— Camila Reyes

Erik, Camila — quick legal note and a draft DPA snippet attached (DPA_addendum_region_pin_draft.docx). High level:

- Proposed clause language: we suggest calling out two explicit, limited exceptions to EU-only processing: "(1) automated failover for no longer than 72 hours; (2) scheduled maintenance windows with customer consent not exceeding 24 hours, except where mutually agreed otherwise."
- Auditability: clause includes requirement for a post-incident affidavit and activation log (timestamped, route, tenant id).
- KMS: include optional BYOK paragraph and a default statement that hosted customers may request split-key escrow; we will not perform key export without customer approval.

Erik — thanks for the prompt. Ops confirmation and attachments below. See attached transient_egress_playbook_v2.pdf for full runbook. Key operational points here:

Summary of transient egress behavior:
- Triggering events: (A) automated regional failover due to regional outage, (B) planned maintenance with customer opt-in, (C) regulatory/legal hold requiring temporary routing.
- Max emergency window: 72 hours by default. Automated healing attempts are made every 15 minutes; if healing does not complete within 72 hours, the incident escalates to on-call and we vendor-lock to customer SLA (we can negotiate longer windows for Dedicated/Private).
- Telemetry & logs: we emit the following per-activation: activation_timestamp, affected_project_id, source_region, destination_region, duration_seconds, triggered_by, incident_ref. Retention: 18 months for residency activations; 12 months for detailed packet-level telemetry (summary only to customers).
- KMS: BYOK supported for Private and Dedicated; for Hosted, we offer customer-managed key wrapping via our KMIP bridge. Keys never leave customer-controlled HSM without explicit consent.
- Controls during window: requests are limited to metadata and inference (no raw backup export without explicit consent). All cross-region sessions are TLS 1.3 and logged for audit.

Operational ask for Medico:
- Please confirm whether Medico requires a hard contractual prohibition against any transient cross-region processing (i.e., absolute EU-only) or whether the two exceptions above are acceptable with addendum language.
- If acceptable, sign the DocuSign authorization for scheduled maintenance windows here: https://docusign.example.com/MD-RES-89012 (placeholder).

Attachments: transient_egress_playbook_v2.pdf (runbook), residency_runbook_v1.pdf (ops summary).

Happy to run through the playbook on a call; I can bring an engineer to walk through the audit logs and a sample activation trace.

— Ben Carter
